name: Morchella importuna

size_cm.note: cap width 2 to 9 cm; the cap is 3 to 15 cm tall on a stem 3 to 10 cm high

notes: An ascomycete that forms sclerotia [23]. Reported (unchecked) to be field-cultivated in China with external nutrient bags and to have a sequenced genome.

tip_speed.source: Elso M, Sanz-Rocha M, Escobar-Hernandez T, Guillen Y, Gerding M, Chavez D, Machuca A 2026, In vitro physiological characterization of strains from transcontinental and endemic Morchella species from south-central Chile, Journal of Fungi 12(8):572
tip_speed.note: Radial growth of nearly 13 mm/day for M. importuna strains I2 and I115 on CYM agar, pH 7, 24 C (13 x 41.7 = 542 um/h). Agrees with strain M04 at 23 C: 0.45 mm/h on glucose CYM and 0.49 to 0.55 mm/h on straw, sawdust and wheat media (Cai et al. 2021, Frontiers in Microbiology 12:636344, https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/microbiology/articles/10.3389/fmicb.2021.636344/full). The same Chilean strain reached 21.1 mm/day at pH 8.5. Replaces the earlier genus figure of 860

uptake_rate.note: tuning value, set to tip speed / segment length so that one feeding segment can supply about one growing tip; no measurement found

t_opt.note: No fitted optimum found. Fastest growth of 13 Morchella strains on PDA was at 20 and 25 C, with growth significantly inhibited at 30 C (Yue et al. 2024, Journal of Fungi 10(3):178, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10971721/); two Chilean M. importuna strains kept getting faster up to 28 C, the highest temperature tested (Elso M, Sanz-Rocha M, Escobar-Hernandez T, Guillen Y, Gerding M, Chavez D, Machuca A 2026, In vitro physiological characterization of strains from transcontinental and endemic Morchella species from south-central Chile, Journal of Fungi 12(8):572, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13514834/). 24 C sits between the two results

t_min.note: No measured lower limit. Mycelium still grows, thin and sparse, at 5 C (Yue et al. 2024, Journal of Fungi 10(3):178, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10971721/) and field spawn running is reported at 2 to 20 C (Hao et al. 2019, AMB Express 9:103, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6626090/), so the limit is put just below, at 0 C

cold_drop.note: Cultivation practice, not a controlled test: mycelium is grown at about 20 C, the beds pass a cold stage of 1 to 3 C for 30 to 40 days, primordia form when the soil returns to 6 to 8 C, and day-night swings of more than 10 C are said to stimulate primordia (Hao et al. 2019, AMB Express 9:103, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6626090/). 10 C is that swing
